analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts for the threat-review scanner: .github/scripts/test-threat-diagnostics.py and .github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py. Neither touches provider runtime code, coordinator contracts, keys, attestation or cache storage. T-041, the only retained definition supplied, is not affected. I found no regression in the provider threat model.

In test-threat-diagnostics.py (head lines 186-187, 196), the integration test now mocks scanner.paid.plan_calls and asserts plans == [2, 1]. This is a test-only assertion about call planning and exposes no data.

In test-threat-model-review.py (head lines 743, 752-760), the workflow-boundary test now asserts:
- THREAT_REVIEW_BASE_SHA is taken only from github.event.pull_request.base.sha, with no env fallback. This tightens pinning of the canonical base.
- timeout-minutes is 60, with THREAT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 3000.
- BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY is workload with a 100-call cap, and BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_CALLS is absent.
- The review job contains no workflow_dispatch, and pr_number and review_depth do not appear in the workflow. This blocks manual inputs from steering a secret-bearing run.

These assertions constrain the workflow and do not weaken any control. The raised timeout and call cap are availability and cost parameters that the tests bound.

Limit: the workflow file .github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml and the scanner modules (budget_scan, call policy) were not supplied. Whether the actual workflow matches these assertions, and whether the paid-call planner enforces the 100-call workload cap, is unverified here. That is a review question for whoever sees those files, not a finding against these test changes.
